description:
Matt Pocock's new Wayfinder skill takes a loose, foggy idea and turns it into a full implementation plan — by breaking the work into decision tickets and resolving them across separate agent sessions. So I used it to plan a game I've been kicking around.

🧠 Run agents? Give them a knowledge base. Agent Wikis has free, curated LLM wikis on a ton of AI topics — plus a Pro tier ($9.99/mo) for super-sized wikis with way more depth: https://agentwikis.com/

Sign up for my FREE weekly newsletter, where I spill my unfiltered thoughts on the latest AI news, cool research, and projects I'm building: https://www.onchainaigarage.com/

Wayfinder is a heavier sibling to Matt Pocock's popular Grill Me skill: instead of one long question session, it charts a "map" of decisions, spins up research/grilling/prototype tickets, and works them in parallel sessions before producing a single implementation handoff. My first time using it, I point it at a rough concept — a pixel-art puzzle platformer where you prompt an AI companion that runs on a limited token budget each stage — and let it interrogate me, run its own research, build prototypes, and scope a vertical slice. I run the whole thing in the Hermes Agent desktop app on GPT-5.6 Terra, then walk through the roadmap it hands off for a coding agent to build from.

description:
Hermes Agent is powerful, but the hard part is knowing what to actually give it.

In this video, I show the exact system I would use to set up Hermes Agent as a daily assistant. Instead of starting with random one-off prompts, I make Hermes interview me, audit my work, build a delegation map, choose the first three workflows, schedule a morning check-in, and turn repeated work into reusable skills.

The goal is not to automate your entire life on day one. The goal is to create a small daily loop where Hermes learns what matters, suggests useful work, handles the safe parts, and slowly becomes more personalized over time.

I also share the prompts I use so you can copy them into your own Hermes Agent.
